comment: Weekly doctrine-build additions, appended by the scheduled IE-SYNC doctrine builder. Merged onto the generated catalog by lib/military-library.ts; do not edit military-library.generated.json directly. Each entry's URL was verified reachable (curl -sL, HTTP 200, application/pdf, plausible size) at the time it was added. This session's outbound network policy allowlisted only csis-website-prod.s3.amazonaws.com; other publisher domains (rand.org, gao.gov, armypubs.army.mil, nato.int, congress.gov, esd.whs.mil, state.gov, stratcomcoe.org, swfound.org) returned proxy 403s and were skipped rather than added unverified.

sources.title: Countering Russian and Chinese Influence Activities
sources.author: CSIS International Security Program
sources.notes: Field-based comparison of Russian influence activity in the UK/Germany and Chinese influence activity in Japan/Australia — a baseline for recognizing adversary IO patterns in allied countries.

sources.title: Influence and Escalation: Implications of Russian and Chinese Influence Operations for Crisis Management
sources.author: CSIS Project on Nuclear Issues
sources.notes: Eight crisis scenarios showing how Russian and Chinese influence operations could complicate U.S. detection, response, and escalation management.

sources.title: Wars of Influence: Expanding U.S. Unclassified Intelligence Reporting on China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea
sources.author: Anthony H. Cordesman, CSIS
sources.notes: Makes the case for expanded unclassified U.S. government reporting as an information-domain tool of strategic competition — relevant to open-source narrative-building.

sources.title: Significant Cyber Incidents
sources.author: CSIS Strategic Technologies Program
sources.notes: Running, dated log of major state-linked cyber incidents since 2006 — a quick-reference baseline for cyber/EMS threat framing.

sources.title: Russia's Shadow War Against the West
sources.author: Seth G. Jones, CSIS
sources.notes: Catalogs Russian sabotage, disinformation, and hybrid actions against Western states below the threshold of war — frames the deterrence gap in the gray zone.

sources.title: By Other Means Part II: Adapting to Compete in the Gray Zone
sources.author: Kathleen H. Hicks et al., CSIS International Security Program
sources.notes: Foundational framework for U.S. gray-zone competition, including information and influence lines of effort — widely cited by IO/OIE planners.

sources.title: How Russia Is Reshaping Command and Control for AI-Enabled Warfare
sources.author: Kateryna Bondar, CSIS Wadhwani AI Center
sources.notes: Details Russia's Glaz/Groza reconnaissance-strike software chain compressing sensor-to-shooter timelines — directly relevant to the C2/decision-cycle fight.

sources.title: The Geometry of Coercion: Tracking the PRC's Maritime and Air Pressure on Taiwan
sources.author: Jose M. Macias III and Benjamin Jensen, CSIS Futures Lab
sources.notes: Spatial-temporal tracking methodology for PLA maritime and air coercion signals around Taiwan — a model for open-source ISR pattern-of-life analysis.

sources.title: Blurred Orbits: Inside China's Commercial Space Expansion
sources.author: Kari A. Bingen, Aidan Powers-Riggs, and Chantal Li, CSIS Aerospace Security Project
sources.notes: Maps China's civil-military-fused commercial space industrial base (launch, satellite manufacturing, remote sensing) — context for space threat and gray-zone assessments.
